questions.q: What is the main advantage of a Plotly chart over a static matplotlib image?
options: It is always more accurate
It can be hovered, zoomed and filtered by the reader
It never needs axis labels
It uses less memory
questions.explain: Plotly charts are interactive: tooltips show exact values, you can zoom and pan, and clicking legend entries toggles groups.

questions.q: What does hover_data=["age", "region"] do in px.scatter?
options: Filters the data to only the age and region columns
Draws age and region as separate axes
Adds those columns to the tooltip shown when hovering over a point
Sorts the data by age and region
questions.explain: hover_data adds extra columns to the tooltip, so the reader sees more context about each point.

questions.q: What is the difference between update_traces and update_layout?
options: There is no difference
update_traces adjusts the whole chart; update_layout adjusts one mark
update_traces saves the chart; update_layout displays it
update_traces adjusts the marks (for example marker size); update_layout adjusts the chart as a whole (for example template and legend title)
questions.explain: Traces are the drawn data marks; layout covers everything around them such as titles, template, legend and margins.

questions.q: How can you share a Plotly chart with someone who has no Python installed?
options: Save it with fig.write_html("chart.html") and send the file, which opens in any browser
Send them the DataFrame
It is impossible; Plotly charts only run in Python
Convert it to a matplotlib figure first
questions.explain: write_html produces a self-contained web page with the interactive chart embedded.

questions.q: When is a static chart usually a better choice than an interactive one?
options: During early data exploration
When building a notebook dashboard for others to explore
When the chart goes into a printed report, slide or PDF, where you control exactly what the reader sees
Never; interactive charts are always better
questions.explain: Interactivity does not survive print or PDF, and a static chart lets you decide exactly what the reader sees.
